'''Paolo Napoleon James Banchero'''<ref name=duke_profile>{{Cite web |title=Paolo Banchero – 2021–22 – Men's Basketball |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/paolo-banchero/17230 |access-date=June 24, 2022 |website=Duke University |language=en}}</ref> ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|p|aʊ|l|oʊ|_|b|æ|ŋ|ˈ|k|ɛər|oʊ}} {{respell|POW|loh|_|bang|KAIR|oh}},<ref>{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3OuDxldBaSA|title=NBA 2K22: Paolo Banchero Gets Scanned In Game |publisher= [[NBA 2K]] |date=March 18, 2022|access-date=May 19, 2022|time=0:04}}</ref> {{IPA|it|ˈpaːolo baŋˈkɛːro|lang}}; born November 12, 2002) is an American and Italian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. Banchero was named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|Rookie of the Year]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) in 2022. Following his freshman season, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], where he was selected with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] by the [[Orlando Magic]]. Banchero was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] in 2023.

==Early life==
Banchero was born in [[Seattle]], Washington. He grew up in the [[Southend Seattle|South Seattle]] neighborhood of [[Mount Baker, Seattle|Mount Baker]].<ref name=duke_profile/> 

Banchero's mother, [[Rhonda Banchero]] (née Smith), played college basketball for [[Washington Huskies women's basketball|Washington]] Huskies women's basketball, leaving as the program's all-time scoring leader. She was a third-round selection in the [[2000 WNBA draft]] and played professionally in the [[American Basketball League (1996–1998)|American Basketball League]] and overseas. Rhonda subsequently became a basketball coach at [[Holy Names Academy]] in Seattle<ref name=mother/><ref name=allen/> and taught young Paolo the game.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3370018/2022/06/21/banchero-ivey-sochan-washington-moms/ | title=Moms taught Banchero, Ivey, Sochan and Washington the game. Now they're top NBA Draft prospects | work=The New York Times | date=June 24, 2022 | last1=Schiffer | first1=Alex | last2=Tucker | first2=Kyle }}</ref>  Banchero's father, Mario, and his uncle played [[college football]] for [[Washington Huskies football|Washington]]. His parents met while attending the [[University of Washington]].<ref name=parrish/> He has a younger brother, Giulio,<ref name="auto">{{cite web | url=https://seattlemedium.com/odea-football-banchero-championship/ | title=O'Dea's Giulio "Lio" Banchero Charts His Own Path In Family Football Legacy | work=The Seattle Medium | date=October 29, 2025 | last=Doyal | first=Kiara }}</ref> and a younger sister, Mia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mia Banchero - 2024 - Women's Soccer |url=https://queensathletics.com/sports/womens-soccer/roster/mia-banchero/11657 |access-date=2026-04-04|website=Queens University of Charlotte Athletics |language=en}}</ref> 

Banchero is of African-American descent on his mother's side and Italian descent on his father's side.<ref name=bennett/> Paolo reached a height of {{convert|3|ft|1}} at 15 months of age.<ref name="mother">{{cite web |last=Glass |first=Gregg |title=Flashback: Rhonda Smith Franklin, Class of 1992 |url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/?date=20040302&slug=flashback02 |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=March 2, 2004}}</ref> 

In his childhood, he played basketball and [[American football]] and took part in [[track and field|track]].<ref name="egan">{{cite web |last=Egan |first=Chris |title=O'Dea basketball star Paolo Banchero getting national attention |url=https://www.king5.com/article/sports/high-school/prep-zone-odea-basketball-star-paolo-banchero-getting-national-attention/281-4062dd68-5018-4f91-a2ac-d93d921e2a1c |publisher=[[KING-TV]] |access-date=April 27, 2020 |date=February 13, 2020}}</ref> He grew up playing basketball at Rotary Boys and Girls Club of Seattle, as well as EBC Camps most notably the "Ballislife Jr. All-American Camp", drawing inspiration from his mother, who played professionally. In seventh grade, Banchero grew from {{height|ft=6|in=1}} to {{height|ft=6|in=5}}.<ref name="allen">{{cite web |last=Allen |first=Aaron |title=Paolo Banchero's Humility And Leadership Has Led Him To A Stellar Season |url=https://seattlemedium.com/paolo-bancheros-humility-leadership-led-stellar-season/ |website=[[Seattle Medium]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=February 12, 2020}}</ref> He was ranked among the top 50 eighth-graders nationally in both basketball and football.<ref name="mireporter">{{cite web |title=Mercer Island student nationally ranked in two sports |url=https://www.mi-reporter.com/sports/mercer-island-student-nationally-ranked-in-two-sports/ |website=[[Mercer Island Reporter]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=May 8, 2017}}</ref>

Banchero's mother helped him file a lawsuit in 2019 against the [[King County Sheriff's Office|King County Sheriff’s Office]] after an officer pointed a gun at a friend of his during a traffic stop after a concert in 2018. Banchero was in the passenger seat of the vehicle during the interaction. The sheriff's office apologized to the two African American high-school students and implemented new use-of-force guidelines to be used when its officers approach motorists. Banchero received $20,000 from the lawsuit.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carter |first=Mike |date=2019-09-05 |title=King County sheriff will apologize to 2 black teens held at gunpoint, pay $80K |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/law-justice/king-county-sheriff-will-apologize-to-2-black-teens-held-at-gunpoint-settles-lawsuit-for-80k/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704204107/https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/law-justice/king-county-sheriff-will-apologize-to-2-black-teens-held-at-gunpoint-settles-lawsuit-for-80k/ |archive-date=2022-07-04 |access-date=2025-02-17 |website=The Seattle Times}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |date=2022-04-01 |title=For Duke’s Paolo Banchero, Mom is the catalyst for his success, personal growth |url=https://andscape.com/features/for-dukes-paolo-banchero-mom-is-the-catalyst-for-his-success-personal-growth/ |access-date=2025-02-17 |website=Andscape |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Banchero was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. Although he received offers from top [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], most recruiting analysts predicted that he would commit to [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].<ref name="parrish">{{cite web |last=Parrish |first=Gary |title=Duke, Kentucky and UNC are recruiting Paolo Banchero, but family ties to Washington make his choice tough |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/duke-kentucky-and-unc-are-recruiting-paolo-banchero-but-family-ties-to-washington-make-his-choice-tough/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=July 31, 2019}}</ref> Despite the predictions, on August 20, 2020, Banchero committed to playing college basketball for Duke.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29707146|title=Duke gets commitment from Paolo Banchero|last=Medcalf|first=Myron|date=August 20, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=June 13, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dukebasketballreport.com/2020/8/20/21376879/duke-recruiting-paolo-banchero-commits-duke-basketball|title=Duke Recruiting: Paolo Banchero commits|last=King|first=JD|date=August 20, 2020|website=Duke Basketball Report|access-date=November 6, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/odea-basketball-star-paolo-banchero-commits-to-duke-over-uw/|title=O'Dea basketball star Paolo Banchero commits to Duke over UW|last=Allen|first=Percy|date=August 20, 2020|website=[[The Seattle Times]]|access-date=November 6, 2023}}</ref>

== Professional career ==

=== Orlando Magic (2022–present) ===
==== 2022–2023: Rookie of the Year ====
Banchero was selected with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-paolo-banchero-first-overall-pick-in-nba-draft-20220623|title=Oh, Paolo! Magic Select Banchero with First Overall Pick in 2022 NBA Draft|website=nba.com|last=Savage|first=Dan|date=June 23, 2022|access-date=July 10, 2022}}</ref> During the draft at that time, it was a surprising selection as the Magic were reported to be taking [[Jabari Smith Jr.]] with their pick. He made his [[2022 NBA Summer League]] debut on July 7 against the [[Houston Rockets]] with 17 points, four rebounds and six assists in a 91–77 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-paolo-banchero-reacts-to-showing-out-in-summer-league-debut-vs-jabari-smith-rockets/|title=Paolo Banchero reacts to showing out in Summer League debut vs. Jabari Smith, Rockets|website=ClutchPoints|last=Salao|first=Renzo|date=July 7, 2022|access-date=July 10, 2022}}</ref> On October 3, 2022, Banchero made his preseason debut, putting up eight points, two rebounds and one assist in a 109–97 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-paolo-bancheros-preseason-debut-will-leave-dejounte-murray-smirking/|title=Magic forward Paolo Banchero's preseason debut will leave Dejounte Murray smirking|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|website=ClutchPoints|date=October 3, 2022|access-date=October 6, 2022}}</ref> On October 19, Banchero made his regular-season debut, putting up 27 points, nine rebounds, five assists and two blocks in a 113–109 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Banchero also became the first player since [[LeBron James]] to put up at least 25 points, five rebounds and five assists in an NBA debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-paolo-bancheros-epic-debut-matches-rare-lebron-james-rookie-feat/|title=Paolo Banchero's epic debut matches rare LeBron James rookie feat|website=ClutchPoints|last=Villas|first=Rexwell|date=October 19, 2022|access-date=October 19, 2022}}</ref> On November 5, Banchero put up 33 points and 16 rebounds in a 126–123 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]]. He also became the second teenager in NBA history to put up at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a game, joining LeBron James.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-paolo-bancheros-latest-feat-only-ever-done-by-lebron-james/|title=Paolo Banchero's latest feat only ever done by LeBron James|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|date=November 5, 2022|access-date=November 5, 2022}}</ref> At the season's end, Banchero was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] and earned [[NBA All-Rookie Team]] honors.<ref>{{cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=April 26, 2023 |title=Paolo Banchero named 2022–23 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year |url=https://www.nba.com/news/paolo-banchero-named-2022-23-kia-nba-rookie-of-the-year |access-date=May 8, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=May 9, 2023 |title=Paolo Banchero headlines 2022–23 Kia NBA All-Rookie teams |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-23-all-rookie-teams-announced |access-date=June 26, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==== 2023–2024: First All-Star Game and playoff appearances ====

On November 2, 2023, Banchero put up 30 points alongside a game-winning layup in a 115–113 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-paolo-banchero-mindset-game-winning-drive-finish-orlando-hard-fought-win-over-jazz|title=Paolo Banchero reveals game-winning mindset as Magic top Jazz|website=ClutchPoints|last=Sampson|first=Peter|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=November 4, 2023}}</ref> On November 4, Banchero recorded a 25-point and 10-assist [[double-double]] while adding seven rebounds and leading the Magic to a 120–101 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Scanlon | first=Dick | title=Magic rout short-handed Lakers 120-101 | website=NBC Los Angeles | date=2023-11-04 | url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/sports/magic-rout-over-shorthanded-lakers-120-101/3260910/ | access-date=2025-06-13}}</ref> On November 15, Banchero posted 17 points, nine rebounds, and made a game-winner in a 96–94 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite game-winner|website=ClutchPoints|last=Smith|first=Christopher|date=November 15, 2023|access-date=November 15, 2023}}</ref> On December 6, Banchero put up a then career-high 42 points in a 121–111 loss |date=March 21, 2024 |access-date=March 21, 2024 }}</ref>

On April 20, Banchero played in his first career postseason game, recording 24 points, 7 rebounds and 5 assists, however committing nine turnovers in a 97–83 loss in Game 1 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs|First Round]] to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url= https://www.si.com/nba/magic/news/magic-cavaliers-2024-nba-playoffs-game-1-final-score-recap|title=Magic Offense Struggles Mightily in Game 1 Loss vs. Cavs|magazine=Sports Illustrated|last=Brener|first=Jeremy|date=April 20, 2024|access-date=April 27, 2024}}</ref> Trailing 2–0 heading into Game 3, Banchero led Orlando to a 121–83 dominant victory over Cleveland behind his 31-point, 14-rebound performance.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5448079/2024/04/26/paolo-banchero-orlando-magic-cavs-game-3/ |title=Paolo Banchero delivers Game 3 star turn he promised Magic teammates|website=TheAthletic|last=Robbins|first=Josh|date=April 26, 2024|access-date=April 27, 2024}}</ref> In Game 5, Banchero scored a playoff career-high 39 points, along with eight rebounds and four assists in a 104–103 narrow loss to the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 30, 2024 |title=Evan Mobley has huge block in final seconds as Cavaliers hold off Banchero, Magic 104-103 in Game 5 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401655121 |access-date=May 5, 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Orlando would go on to lose to Cleveland in seven games despite Banchero's 38-point and playoff career-high 16-rebound outing in the 106–94 close-out loss in Game 7.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 5, 2024 |title=Donovan Mitchell scores 39 points as Cavaliers push past Magic 106-94 in Game 7 to get Boston next |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401655123 |access-date=May 5, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==== 2024–2025: Injury and return ====
On October 23, 2024, in the Magic's season-opening game, Banchero put up 33 points and 11 rebounds in a 116–97 win over the [[Miami Heat]]. He joined [[Shaquille O'Neal]] and [[Tracy McGrady]] as the only players in Magic franchise history to put up at least 30 points and 10 rebounds in a season-opening game.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-paolo-banchero-joins-shaquille-oneal-tracy-mcgrady-opening-night|title= Paolo Banchero joins Shaquille O'Neal, Tracy McGrady with stellar opening night|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ojeda|first=Julian|date=October 23, 2024|access-date=October 23, 2024}}</ref> On October 28, Banchero put up a career-high 50 points, along with 13 rebounds, nine assists and two blocks in a 119–115 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/magic-news-paolo-bancheros-stat-line-pacers-first-kind-nba-history|title=Paolo Banchero's stunning stat line vs. Pacers is first of its kind in NBA history|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}}</ref> Banchero's 50-point performance made him the fourth player in Orlando Magic history to score at least 50 points in a single game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Orlando Magic Single Game Points Leaders |url=https://doyoubelievein.basketball/magic/stats/single-game-points/ |access-date=January 2, 2025 |website=Do You Believe in Basketball}}</ref>

On October 30, while playing against the [[Chicago Bulls]], Banchero suffered a torn oblique on his right side. Banchero later stated that he played through the pain, only receiving medical attention after Orlando's loss. On November 1, hours before a game against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Banchero's diagnosis was made public. He was expected to be re-examined four to six weeks following the initial diagnosis, and to sit out indefinitely.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-31 |title=Magic star Banchero sidelined with torn oblique |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42116980 |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-01 |title=Injury Update: Paolo Banchero |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/videos/paolo-banchero-orlando-magic-cleveland-cavaliers-injury-update-interview-20241101 |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> Banchero returned on January 10, 2025, posting 34 points and seven rebounds in a 109–106 loss against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-11 |title=Paolo Banchero scores 34 in return to Magic lineup after 34-game absence |url=https://www.nba.com/news/banchero-returns-to-magic-lineup |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 20, Banchero put up 36 points, 10 rebounds, and five assists in a 114–108 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He joined O'Neal and McGrady as the only players in Magic franchise history to put up multiple games with at least 35 points, 10 rebounds, and five assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/orlando-magic/magic-news-paolo-banchero-joins-shaquille-neal-tracy-mcgrady-epic-franchise-club|title=Magic's Paolo Banchero joins Shaquille O'Neal, Tracy McGrady in epic franchise club|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=February 20, 2025|access-date=February 20, 2025}}</ref>

==== 2025–2026: Contract extension ====
On July 7, 2025, Banchero signed a five-year, $239 million contract extension with the Magic.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Paolo Banchero, Magic agree to five-year rookie max extension|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45690598/paolo-banchero-magic-agree-five-year-rookie-max-extension|access-date=July 16, 2025|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> 

On December 18, Banchero recorded his third career triple-double with 26 points, 16 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 126–115 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810232|title=Nuggets' Jokic breaks Kareem's record for career assists by center|website=ESPN.com|date=December 18, 2025|access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref> On December 29, Banchero posted his fourth career triple-double with 23 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists in a tight 107–106 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810306|title=Jamal Shead scores 19 as Raptors overcome 21-point deficit to beat Magic 107-106 |website=ESPN.com|date=December 29, 2025|access-date=December 29, 2025}}</ref> 

On April 29, 2026, in Game 5 of the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(1) Detroit Pistons vs. (8) Orlando Magic|first-round playoff series]], Banchero recorded a career-high 45 points, along with 9 rebounds and 7 assists, but the Magic fell 116–109 to the [[2025–26 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Pistons vs. Magic Game 5 takeaways: Detroit pushes Orlando to the brink |website=NBA.com |date=April 29, 2026 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/pistons-magic-2026-playoffs-game-5-takeaways |access-date=May 1, 2026}}</ref> In Game 7, despite Banchero posting 38 points, nine rebounds, and six assists, the Magic were eliminated from the playoffs with a 116–94 loss to the Pistons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Pistons vs. Orlando Magic - Game Recap - April 2026 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401869418/magic-pistons |website=ESPN.com |access-date=May 3, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
Banchero was eligible to play for the [[Italy men's national basketball team|Italy national team]] and indicated his willingness to represent Italy in international competitions.<ref>{{cite news |date=November 27, 2021 |title=Paolo Banchero: 'I'm excited to play for Italy' |url=https://basketnews.com/news-160608-paolo-banchero-im-excited-to-play-for-italy.html |access-date=May 18, 2022 |work=BasketNews.com |language=en}}</ref> He was selected to their 24-man squad for the [[EuroBasket 2022]] qualification games in November 2020; however, he did not play.<ref>{{cite news |date=November 2, 2020 |title=Ambitious Banchero waits in the wings for Italy |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/eurobasket-2022-qualifiers-news-ambitious-banchero-waits-in-the-wings-for-italy |access-date=January 2, 2025 |work=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref> In June 2023, Banchero opted to play for the [[2023 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2023 U.S. national team]] at the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Rasmussen |first=Karl |date=June 26, 2023 |title=Paolo Banchero's Team USA Decision Drew Irate Response From Italian Basketball Federation President |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/06/26/paolo-banchero-team-usa-decision-drew-irate-response-italian-basketball-president |access-date=June 27, 2023 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> He said that his mother had played for Team USA, so it was always his dream.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Vardon |first=Joe |date=August 3, 2023 |title=Inside Paolo Banchero's decision to play for Team USA over Italy: 'He fooled us' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4747845/2023/08/03/paolo-banchero-usa-italy-fiba-world-cup/ |access-date=August 27, 2023 |work=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref> [[Gianni Petrucci]], president of the [[Italian Basketball Federation]], described Banchero's decision as "betrayal."<ref>{{cite web |last=Henderson |first=Cydney |date=June 27, 2023 |title=Paolo Banchero 'fooled us' by deciding to play for USA, Italian basketball president says |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/magic/2023/06/27/paolo-banchero-slammed-by-italy-basketball-ditching-for-team-usa/70362394007/ |access-date=August 27, 2023 |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

==Business endeavors==
In November 2025, Banchero joined the ownership group of the [[Seattle Seawolves]]. He also has stakes in [[AC Milan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NBA All Star Paolo Banchero Joins Seattle Seawolves Ownership Group |url=https://www.seawolves.rugby/news/nba-all-star-paolo-banchero-joins-seattle-seawolves-ownership-group |website=seawolves.rugby |access-date=14 November 2025 |language=en |date=13 November 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In February 2020, Banchero received Italian citizenship because of his paternal ancestry.<ref name="evans">{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Jayda |title=First, state for O'Dea's Paolo Banchero. Next, the world? |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/star-times-boys-basketball-first-state-for-odeas-paolo-banchero-next-the-world/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=April 26, 2020 |date=March 2, 2020}}</ref>

On the morning of November 14, 2021, Banchero was charged with aiding and abetting [[DUI]] after [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] teammate Michael Savarino, grandson of coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]], was arrested on DUI charges.<ref name="Borzello">{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Duke basketball player Michael Savarino, grandson of coach Mike Krzyzewski, faces DUI charges along with Paolo Banchero |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32643987 |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=November 16, 2021 |date=November 16, 2021}}</ref> On July 29, 2022, the charges against Banchero were dropped after Savarino pled guilty to DUI.<ref>{{cite web |last=ESPN Staff |title=Orlando Magic's Paolo Banchero has DWI-related charge against him dropped |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34311683 |access-date=April 27, 2023 |website=ESPN.com|date=July 29, 2022 }}</ref>

On May 8, 2022, Banchero attended the inaugural [[Miami Grand Prix]] in [[Miami Gardens, Florida|Miami Gardens]]. There, he was interviewed by [[Sky Sports]] announcer [[Martin Brundle]], who mistakenly believed that he was [[Patrick Mahomes]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |date=May 8, 2022 |title=This F1 announcer thought he was talking to Patrick Mahomes. It was really Paolo Banchero |url=https://www.sbnation.com/2022/5/8/23062687/f1-interview-patrick-mahomes-paolo-banchero-martin-brundle |access-date=June 24, 2022 |website=SBNation.com |language=en}}</ref> 

Banchero's paternal cousin, [[Chris Banchero]],<ref name="ramos">{{cite web |last=Ramos |first=Gerry |title=Chris Banchero says sky's the limit for cousin Paolo |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/chris-banchero-says-sky-s-the-limit-for-cousin-paolo-a793-20220720/ |website=[[Spin.ph]] |access-date=July 20, 2022 |date=July 20, 2022}}</ref> is a professional basketball player for the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Citation |title=PAANO Na-Impluwensyahan Ni Chris Banchero Si Paolo Sa Basketball |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=utN9_TvuWyw |language=en |website=YouTube | date=June 19, 2022 |access-date=June 20, 2022}}</ref> 

Banchero's younger brother, Giulio, has signed to play college football at [[Eastern Washington Eagles football|Eastern Washington]] starting in 2026.<ref name="auto"/>
